issues.display_title: Issue #1303: Update API AI Blur
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Update the token conversion rate for the AI Blur API.

Endpoint: /tours/ai-blur

Change

The conversion rate was originally set to 1 token = 10 AI tokens, and must be changed to 1 token = 20 AI tokens.

Old New
Conversion rate 1 token = 10 AI tokens 1 token = 20 AI tokens

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Calling /tours/ai-blur consumes tokens at the updated rate of 1 token = 20 AI tokens.
  2. Token deduction/calculation reflects the new rate consistently across the AI Blur flow.
  3. No regression in the AI Blur request/response behavior aside from the updated rate.

Demo from Developer

To see implementation for current token calculation, you can see here: GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4087.

API QA Tester Summary - Issue #1303: Update API AI Blur

Suite: qa_testing/api/tours/issue_1303_update_api_ai_blur_api.spec.js (API contract/static/source validation)
Related FE: https://github.com/GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard/issues/4087 - developer reference for current token calculation
Env: Static validation against current GoThru-API-New checkout on 2026-07-10; live token-purchase/AI Blur request not executed because this would mutate billing/token/blur data

Test Scenario & Result

# Box Scenario Given -> Expected Matrix Result
1 White AI Blur route/controller/action/worker mapping POST /tours/ai-blur -> BlurController@aiBlur -> AIBlur::execute -> RabbitMQ ai_blur worker TP Pass
2 Gray Token provisioning conversion rate Purchased token rows -> each token should be provisioned with ai_tokens = 20 FN Fail
3 Black AI Blur deduction consistency AI Blur allocation/worker should consume the token row's ai_tokens - ai_tokens_used capacity and reject insufficient payload credits TP Pass
4 Task Sprint #1303 acceptance Consumption can use per-row capacity, but newly purchased tokens are not explicitly created with 20 AI tokens TP + FN Fail

API Status Code & Contract Review

Flow: token purchase (Stripe/PayPal BuyToken) -> BuyTokenHelpers::processTokenPurchaseSuccess() -> tokens rows -> POST /tours/ai-blur -> AIBlur::allocateBlurTokensByUsageType() -> RabbitMQ ai_blur worker -> tokens.ai_tokens_used

API result HTTP/body status Response contract Review
Success 200 / statusCode: 200 data.messages success envelope after queue publish Source route/controller verified
Validation error 409 invalid panos, moderation_id, user_agree, or type returns response envelope Source validation verified
Not enough tokens 409 messages.tokens.not_enough when allocated token capacity cannot cover paid blur credits Source allocation verified
Token conversion N/A source provisioning each purchased token row should carry 20 AI-token capacity Failed: purchase insert does not set ai_tokens

Evidence

  • Network Fetch/XHR list screenshot: Not captured; backend-only static validation, no live billing/token mutation performed.
  • Headers screenshot: Not captured.
  • Payload screenshot: Not captured.
  • Response/Preview screenshot: Not captured.
  • CLI/test output:
    • Command: node node_modules\@playwright\test\cli.js test --config=.\playwright.config.js --grep "#1303"
    • Result: Failed at Gray Box token provisioning check.
    • Failure: BuyTokenHelpers::processTokenPurchaseSuccess() inserts token rows with token_type, token_price, user_id, and date_expire, but no ai_tokens => 20 value.
  • Logs/API notes:
    • /tours/ai-blur route is present and maps to Tours\Blur\BlurController@aiBlur.
    • AIBlur::allocateBlurTokensByUsageType() reads real row capacity from ai_tokens - ai_tokens_used; it no longer hardcodes 10 credits during allocation.
    • The ai_blur worker also reads ai_tokens and increments ai_tokens_used by 1 per paid blur row; both consumes 2 rows/credits per paid pano.
    • Remaining-credit endpoint calculates blur remaining credits from ai_tokens - ai_tokens_used.

Bug notes

  • Bug found: token purchase provisioning has not been updated to explicitly create purchased token rows with ai_tokens = 20.
  • Because the task changes the conversion rate from 1 token = 10 AI tokens to 1 token = 20 AI tokens, the source of new token capacity must be updated at token creation time, not only at AI Blur consumption time.
  • Current AI Blur consumption logic is mostly capacity-based, but it can only consume 20 AI tokens if the token row already has ai_tokens = 20. New rows inserted by BuyTokenHelpers::processTokenPurchaseSuccess() do not set that value in the current checkout.

issues.display_title: Issue #1459: Publishing stuck: update_dates unserialize crashes RabbitMQ publishing worker (ConstellationClass)
issues.main_description_html:
Description

New tours stopped publishing. Reported for user_id = 46677 — the user published 711 tours this month, but new tours are no longer publishing, and the tours are not marked to be published.

Root cause (already diagnosed)

There was an issue with update_dates unserialization that was crashing the publishing RabbitMQ worker. When update_dates failed to unserialize into an array, the worker crashed and publishing stalled.

Location: app/Class/ConstellationClass.php (around line 807)

Fix (applied locally, needs to land in git):

$aUpdates = @unserialize(str_replace('%22', '"', $auditId['update_dates']));
if (!is_array($aUpdates)) {
    $aUpdates = [];
}

From the report: "I've fixed the problem with publishing — there was an issue with update-date unserialize that was crashing the publishing rabbitmq worker. Basically you need to update the version from git for /home/jenkins/workspace/gothru-api-live/app/Class/ConstellationClass.php:807."

"I fixed it, but you need to apply the fix in GitHub if that is in git."

Action required

  • Apply / confirm the update_dates unserialize guard fix in app/Class/ConstellationClass.php in the git repo (the live server was hotfixed directly and must be reconciled with git so the next deploy doesn't overwrite it).
  • Verify the publishing RabbitMQ worker no longer crashes on malformed/non-array update_dates.
  • Confirm publishing resumes for user_id 46677 (try publishing the top 2–3 tours) and that tours get correctly marked as published.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The update_dates unserialize guard is committed in git (ConstellationClass.php) so it survives deploys.
  2. The publishing worker processes jobs without crashing when update_dates is malformed or not an array.
  3. New tours for the affected user publish successfully and are marked as published.

Demo from Developer

update_dates protection Passed app/Class/ConstellationClass.php now safely handles malformed or non-array update_dates values before adding a new publish update date.
Live endpoint protection Passed The live publish endpoint rejects requests without authentication before any publish job can be queued.
Production publish confirmation Not executed Publishing the top 2-3 tours for user_id 46677 would modify production data and trigger real publishing, so it was not executed without explicit approval and approved tour data.

Validation Result

Passed for the committed guard and safe live endpoint validation. No regression was found in the guarded update_dates handling.
